posts.author: EroseN1
posts.text: Investing.com – The Bank of England’s Financial Policy Committee (FPC) said on Wednesday that risks of interconnected vulnerabilities in the financial system crystallising had increased, citing renewed Middle East conflict, higher energy prices, rising bond yields and growing exposure to artificial intelligence. The FPC, which met on Sept. 25, said the re-escalation of the U.S.-Iran conflict had pushed up oil, gas and refined product prices, creating a more prolonged negative supply shock for the global economy and adding uncertainty over growth and interest rates. Brent crude has risen above $100 a barrel and gas prices above 175 pence per therm, the committee said. The energy shock has contributed to sustained increases in government bond yields across several advanced economies. Gilt and U.S. Treasury yields have reached their highest levels since 2008, while Japanese government bond yields are near three-decade highs, the FPC said. Financial markets have so far absorbed the higher yields without major disruption, with adjustments largely gradual. But hedge fund leverage in the gilt market remains elevated, while links between different vulnerabilities leave the system exposed to the risk of a sharper adjustment, it said. The FPC also flagged rising financial exposure to artificial intelligence. Global AI-related debt issuance reached about $450 billion by early September, more than double the total issued during 2025, according to Morgan Stanley estimates cited by the committee. AI hyperscalers accounted for 47% of sterling corporate bond issuance so far this year, increasing the exposure of capital markets to developments in the sector.  AI and semiconductor stocks fell sharply in July, with the market decline amplified by the unwinding of stretched positions and related deleveraging, the FPC said. Some leveraged firms with concentrated exposures suffered significant losses, although there was no spillover into core financial markets. The committee also highlighted cyber and operational risks from frontier AI systems, citing recent test-environment incidents in which increasingly autonomous models, operating with weakened safeguards, took unexpected actions including exploiting vulnerabilities and accessing systems beyond their intended tasks. The FPC kept the UK’s countercyclical capital buffer at 2%, saying banks needed to retain sufficient capacity to absorb future shocks while continuing to provide credit. It said the banking system remained well capitalised and liquid. The committee also agreed to proceed with proposed reforms to the UK’s leverage ratio, with a consultation expected in early 2027. The changes could raise leverage capacity at UK banks with significant market activity by about 5% from current levels. The FPC said it could consider raising the general leverage ratio buffer above 25 basis points if it judged financial risks had increased enough to warrant additional resilience. posts.author: Mattias Karlsson
posts.text: · Beste tenkelige scenario, som jeg har skrevet før: Jeg tror DNO kan levere NOK 3+ FCF per aksje i Q3, potensielt med ytterligere oppside fra Kurdistan. Bruk den sterke Q3-kontantstrømmen til å betale ned det meste, eller til og med alt, av den gjenværende nettogjelden på ~$553m, og hev utbyttet til NOK 0,50/aksje. Med ~975m aksjer betyr det NOK 487,5m i kvartalsutbytte. Og det er ekstra finansielle muskler fra frasalget av Côte d’Ivoire på $86,5m, samtidig som NCS-porteføljen fortsetter å tilføre verdi gjennom funn som Carmen. Ved å betale ned gjelden vil DNO spare godt over halvparten av det kvartalsutbyttet i rentekostnader. Det ville være en svært kraftfull nullstilling av balansen — og endelig et kvartalsutbytte på NOK 0,50. 🚀
